content_text: Do NOT say 'Myself Alex' in formal conversations. Always say 'I am Alex' or 'My name is Alex'.

title: The Simple Present Rule
content_text:
We use Simple Present for habits and daily routines.
Formula:
I / You / We / They + Base Verb (e.g., I wake up at 6 AM)
He / She / It + Verb + s/es (e.g., She drinks tea)

title: Textbook Summary & Author Introduction
content:
**Author:** Liam O'Flaherty (1896–1984), a renowned Irish novelist and short-story writer.

**Plot Overview:**
The young seagull was alone on his ledge. His two brothers and his little sister had already learned to fly away the day before. But he was afraid to fly with them. Whenever he took a little run forward to the brink of the ledge and attempted to flap his wings, he became terrified. The great expanse of sea stretched down beneath, and it seemed a long way down — miles down.

His parents called to him shrilly, scolding him, and threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away. But for the life of him he could not move. 

Finally, his mother devised a clever plan. She picked up a piece of fish and flew across to him. Maddened by hunger, the young seagull dived at the fish. As he fell outward into space, a monstrous terror seized him, but in the next moment he felt his wings spread outwards. The wind rushed against his breast feathers. He was no longer falling headlong. He was soaring gradually downwards and outwards. He had made his first flight!

title: Active and Passive Voice Rules & Formulas
content:
### Golden Rules for Transformation:
1. **Identify the Subject (S), Verb (V), and Object (O)**.
2. **Move the Object to the Subject position**.
3. **Change the Verb to suitable 'Be' verb + Past Participle (V3)**.
4. **Add the preposition 'by' before the original Subject**.

### Tense Transformation Table:
• **Simple Present:** *S + V1 + O* ➔ *O + am/is/are + V3 + by + S*
  - Active: *"She writes a letter."*
  - Passive: *"A letter is written by her."*

• **Simple Past:** *S + V2 + O* ➔ *O + was/were + V3 + by + S*
  - Active: *"Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone."*
  - Passive: *"The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell."*

• **Present Continuous:** *S + am/is/are + V(-ing) + O* ➔ *O + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + S*
  - Active: *"The students are decorating the hall."*
  - Passive: *"The hall is being decorated by the students."*

• **Modal Verbs:** *S + can/must/should + V1 + O* ➔ *O + can/must/should + be + V3 + by + S*
  - Active: *"You must complete the assignment."*
  - Passive: *"The assignment must be completed by you."*
tamil_content:
செய்பவரை முதன்மைப்படுத்துவது **செய்வினை (Active Voice)**; செய்யப்பட்ட செயலை அல்லது பொருளை முதன்மைப்படுத்துவது **செயப்பாட்டு வினை (Passive Voice)**.
சூத்திரம்: பொருள் (Object) + Be வினைச்சொல் + வினைச்சொல்லின் 3-ஆம் வடிவம் (V3) + by + எழுவாய் (Subject).

title: 📖 About: Sea Turtles
content_text:
Sea Turtles are ancient marine reptiles that have lived on Earth for over 100 million years — they even survived the extinction of the dinosaurs! Today, they face serious threats from human activities.

Facts about Sea Turtles:
• There are 7 species of sea turtles worldwide
• They can live for 80+ years
• Female turtles return to the same beach where they were born to lay eggs
• A sea turtle's sex is determined by the temperature of the sand
• They migrate thousands of kilometres across oceans

Threats they face:
• Pollution (plastic bags mistaken for jellyfish)
• Climate change (warming sands affect egg hatching)
• Illegal poaching for shells and eggs
• Loss of nesting beaches

title: 📖 About: Eidgah by Premchand
content_text:
"Eidgah" is a touching short story by the great Hindi writer Premchand. It tells the story of Hamid, a poor four-year-old orphan boy, who goes to the Eid fair (Eidgah) with his friends. While all his friends spend their money on sweets and toys, Hamid buys a pair of tongs for his grandmother, who burns her hands while cooking.

Key themes:
• Selfless love and sacrifice
• The wisdom and maturity of children
• Poverty and its effects on childhood
• The joy of giving over receiving

Moral: True love means thinking about others before yourself, even in times of personal desire.

title: 📖 About: Wind on Haunted Hill — Ruskin Bond
content_text:
"Wind on Haunted Hill" by the beloved Indian author Ruskin Bond is an atmospheric short story set in the hills of India. The story builds suspense as characters encounter mysterious winds and strange events on a hill that locals believe is haunted.

About Ruskin Bond:
• Born 1934 in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh
• One of India's most popular English-language authors
• Known for writing about the hills of India with warmth and nostalgia
• Famous works: The Blue Umbrella, Room on the Roof

Key themes:
• Fear and superstition vs rational thinking
• The beauty and mystery of nature
• Courage in the face of the unknown

title: 📖 About: The Nose-Jewel — C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji)
content_text:
"The Nose-Jewel" (மூக்குத்தி) is a short story by C. Rajagopalachari, one of India's greatest statesmen and authors. The story is set in a Tamil village and features Sivasankaran, a young Brahmin who is tricked into buying an expensive nose-jewel for his wife by a cunning merchant.

About C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji):
• 1878–1972
• First Governor-General of independent India
• Last Governor-General of India before the republic
• Founder of Swatantra Party
• Known for his simple yet powerful writing style

Key themes:
• The dangers of greed and vanity
• The cunning of merchants and trust in society
• Village life in Tamil Nadu
• Moral values and consequences of wrong decisions

title: 📖 About: His First Flight — Liam O'Flaherty
content_text:
"His First Flight" is a short story by Irish writer Liam O'Flaherty. A young seagull is afraid to fly even though all his brothers and sisters have already flown away. His parents try to encourage him, but he refuses. His mother tempts him with a piece of fish, and when he tries to reach it, he instinctively begins to fly.

About Liam O'Flaherty:
• Born: 28 August 1896, Inis Mór, Ireland
• Irish writer known for his vivid descriptions of nature
• Major works: The Informer, Skerrett, Famine

Key themes:
• Overcoming fear through courage and necessity
• The importance of taking the first step
• Parental guidance and tough love
• The joy of discovering one's capabilities

Symbolism:
• Young seagull = anyone afraid to take risks
• Flight = achieving one's potential
• Hunger (fish) = motivation to overcome fear
tamil_translation:
"His First Flight" என்பது அயர்லாந்து எழுத்தாளர் Liam O'Flaherty எழுதிய சிறுகதை. ஒரு இளம் கடற்பறவை பறக்க பயந்திருக்கிறது. தன் அன்னை மீனால் தூண்டியதால் அது பறக்கத் தொடங்குகிறது.

• தைரியத்தின் மூலம் பயத்தை வெல்வது

title: 📖 About: Two Gentlemen of Verona — A.J. Cronin
content_text:
"Two Gentlemen of Verona" is a short story by the Scottish author A.J. Cronin. The story is set in post-World War II Italy. The narrator, while travelling through Verona with his driver Luigi, meets two young boys — Nicola and Jacopo — who are trying to earn money by doing various odd jobs.

Later, the narrator discovers that these boys are using all their earnings to pay for their sister Lucia's treatment for spinal tuberculosis in a hospital in Stresa.

About A.J. Cronin:
• Archibald Joseph Cronin (1896–1981)
• Scottish novelist, physician, and short story writer
• Famous works: The Citadel, The Stars Look Down, The Keys of the Kingdom

Key themes:
• Selfless love and sacrifice of siblings
• The devastating effects of war on civilians
• Hope and resilience in the face of adversity
• Dignity of labour — no work is too small

Moral: True love does not seek reward. It silently serves.

title: 📘 What is a Noun?
content_text:
A Noun is a word that names a person, place, animal, thing, or idea. Every sentence contains at least one noun.

👤 Person → Teacher, Ravi, Doctor
🏙️ Place → Chennai, India, School
🐾 Animal → Dog, Tiger, Parrot
📦 Thing → Book, Chair, Pencil
💭 Idea → Happiness, Courage, Love

title: 📗 Types of Nouns
content_text:
1. COMMON NOUN — General name for any person, place, or thing.
   Examples: city, boy, dog, river, teacher

2. PROPER NOUN — Specific name of a person, place, or organisation. Always starts with a capital letter.
   Examples: Chennai, Ravi, Ganges, India

3. ABSTRACT NOUN — Name of a feeling, quality, or idea that you cannot see or touch.
   Examples: happiness, love, courage, wisdom

4. COLLECTIVE NOUN — Name of a group of persons, animals, or things.
   Examples: a flock of birds, a team of players, a pride of lions

   எ.கா: நகரம், ஆண்குழந்தை, நாய்

title: 📘 What is a Pronoun?
content_text:
A Pronoun is a word used in place of a Noun to avoid repetition.

Without pronoun: "Ravi went to school. Ravi was late."
With pronoun: "Ravi went to school. He was late." ✅

Types of Pronouns:
1. PERSONAL → I, You, He, She, It, We, They, Me, Him, Her, Us, Them
2. POSSESSIVE → My, Your, His, Her, Its, Our, Their
3. REFLEXIVE → Myself, Yourself, Himself, Herself, Itself
4. DEMONSTRATIVE → This, That, These, Those
5. INTERROGATIVE → Who, Whom, Which, What, Whose
6. RELATIVE → Who, Whom, Which, That

5. கேள்வி (Interrogative) → Who, Which, What

title: 📘 Adjectives — Describing Words
content_text:
An Adjective is a word that describes or modifies a Noun or Pronoun.

Examples:
• "She has a beautiful house." → beautiful describes house
• "The tall boy ran fast." → tall describes boy

DEGREES OF COMPARISON:
1. POSITIVE — describes one thing (no comparison)
   Format: adjective
   Example: tall, sweet, intelligent

2. COMPARATIVE — compares two things
   Format: adjective + er (short) / more + adjective (long)
   Example: taller, sweeter, more intelligent

3. SUPERLATIVE — compares one among many (highest degree)
   Format: adjective + est (short) / most + adjective (long)
   Example: tallest, sweetest, most intelligent

பெயரடை (Adjective) என்பது பெயர்ச்சொல்லை விவரிக்கும் சொல்.

ஒப்பிட்டு நிலைகள் (Degrees of Comparison):
1. Positive — ஒரு விஷயத்தை மட்டும் விவரிக்கும்: tall, sweet
2. Comparative — இரண்டை ஒப்பிடும்: taller, more intelligent
3. Superlative — பலரில் மேலானவரை குறிக்கும்: tallest, most intelligent

title: 📊 Irregular Comparisons — Must Know!
content_text:
IRREGULAR ADJECTIVES (Do not follow normal rules):

| Positive | Comparative | Superlative |
| Good | Better | Best |
| Bad | Worse | Worst |
| Much/Many | More | Most |
| Little | Less | Least |
| Far | Farther/Further | Farthest/Furthest |
| Old | Elder/Older | Eldest/Oldest |

Rules for SHORT adjectives (1-2 syllables):
• Add -er for Comparative: tall → taller
• Add -est for Superlative: tall → tallest
• Double consonant if needed: big → bigger → biggest

Rules for LONG adjectives (3+ syllables):
• Use "more" for Comparative: more beautiful
• Use "most" for Superlative: most beautiful

| Positive | Comparative | Superlative |
| Good (நல்ல) | Better (மேலான) | Best (சிறந்த) |
| Bad (கெட்ட) | Worse | Worst |
| Many/Much | More | Most |

title: 📘 Types of Sentences
content_text:
SIMPLE SENTENCE — One independent clause with a subject and verb.
Example: "She reads every day."

COMPOUND SENTENCE — Two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So).
Example: "She reads books, and he watches movies."

COMPLEX SENTENCE — One independent clause + one or more dependent clauses joined by subordinating conjunctions (because, when, if, although, since, after, before, while, unless, until).
Example: "She reads every day because she loves stories."

COMPOUND-COMPLEX — Two independent clauses + one dependent clause.
Example: "Although it was raining, she went to school, and she attended all classes."
tamil_translation:
SIMPLE SENTENCE (தனி வாக்கியம்) — ஒரு கர்த்தா, ஒரு வினை.
எ.கா: "She reads every day."

COMPOUND SENTENCE (கூட்டு வாக்கியம்) — இரண்டு தனி வாக்கியங்கள் (and, but, or, so) இணைப்பால் இணைக்கப்படும்.
ெ.கா: "She reads books, and he watches movies."

COMPLEX SENTENCE (கலப்பு வாக்கியம்) — ஒரு தனி வாக்கியம் + சார்பு வாக்கியம் (because, when, if, although).
ெ.கா: "She reads because she loves stories."

title: ✏️ Identifying Sentence Types
content_text:
Identify the sentence type:

1. "The dog barked loudly." → SIMPLE
   (one subject: dog, one verb: barked)

2. "It was hot, so she drank water." → COMPOUND
   (two clauses joined by "so")

3. "Although she was tired, she completed her homework." → COMPLEX
   (dependent clause starts with "although")

4. "She studied hard, and she passed the exam because she was determined." → COMPOUND-COMPLEX

Key Conjunctions:
• Coordinating: and, but, or, nor, for, yet, so
• Subordinating: because, when, if, although, since, before, after

title: 📘 Complete Guide to Tenses
content_text:
PRESENT TENSES:
• Simple Present: She eats rice. (habit/routine)
• Present Continuous: She is eating rice. (happening now)
• Present Perfect: She has eaten rice. (completed, relevant now)
• Present Perfect Continuous: She has been eating rice for an hour. (started past, still happening)

PAST TENSES:
• Simple Past: She ate rice. (completed past action)
• Past Continuous: She was eating rice. (ongoing past action)
• Past Perfect: She had eaten rice before he came. (earlier past action)
• Past Perfect Continuous: She had been eating rice for an hour.

FUTURE TENSES:
• Simple Future: She will eat rice.
• Future Continuous: She will be eating rice.
• Future Perfect: She will have eaten rice by 2 PM.
• Future Perfect Continuous: She will have been eating rice for an hour.
tamil_translation:

• Simple Present: She eats. (பழக்கம்/வழக்கம்)
• Present Continuous: She is eating. (இப்போது நடக்கிறது)
• Present Perfect: She has eaten. (முடிந்தது, இப்போது தொடர்புடையது)

கடந்தகால வகைகள்:
• Simple Past: She ate. (முடிந்த செயல்)
• Past Continuous: She was eating. (கடந்தகாலத்தில் நடந்தது)
• Past Perfect: She had eaten. (முந்திய கடந்தகாலம்)

எதிர்கால வகைகள்:
• Simple Future: She will eat.
• Future Perfect: She will have eaten.

title: 🔑 Signal Words for Each Tense
content_text:
Use these signal words to identify the correct tense:

⏰ PRESENT TENSES:
• Simple: always, usually, often, every day, never, sometimes
• Continuous: now, at this moment, currently, right now, look!
• Perfect: just, already, yet, ever, never, recently, since, for

⏰ PAST TENSES:
• Simple: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 1990
• Perfect: before, by the time, when (past), already (past)

⏰ FUTURE TENSES:
• Simple: tomorrow, next week, soon, in the future
• Perfect: by tomorrow, by next year, by the time

💡 Quick Formula:
• is/am/are + ing = Present Continuous
• has/have + past participle = Present Perfect
• had + past participle = Past Perfect
• will + base verb = Future Simple

• Perfect: just, already, yet, ever, recently

⏰ கடந்தகாலம்:

title: 📘 Prepositions of Time, Place, Direction
content_text:
A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or pronoun to show its relationship with another word in the sentence.

📍 PLACE PREPOSITIONS:
• IN — inside (in the box, in Chennai, in India)
• ON — on a surface (on the table, on the wall)
• AT — specific point (at the station, at home, at school)
• ABOVE/BELOW — higher or lower than
• BEHIND/IN FRONT OF — relative position
• BETWEEN — in the middle of two things
• AMONG — in the middle of many things

⏰ TIME PREPOSITIONS:
• IN — months, years, seasons, long periods (in July, in 2024, in summer, in the morning)
• ON — days and dates (on Monday, on 15th August)
• AT — clock time and specific moments (at 5 PM, at noon, at night)
• FOR — duration (for 3 hours, for two years)
• SINCE — starting point (since 2020, since Monday)
tamil_translation:
Preposition என்பது நாம/இடம் ஆகியவற்றுக்கும் வாக்கியத்தின் மற்ற சொற்களுக்கும் உள்ள உறவை காட்டும் சொல்.

📍 இட உரிச்சொற்கள்:
• IN — உள்ளே (in the box, in Chennai)
• ON — மேற்பரப்பில் (on the table)
• AT — குறிப்பிட்ட இடம் (at the station)

⏰ கால உரிச்சொற்கள்:
• IN — மாதம், ஆண்டு (in July, in 2024)
• ON — நாள்கள் (on Monday)
• AT — நேரம் (at 5 PM, at noon)
• FOR — காலகட்டம் (for 3 hours)
• SINCE — தொடக்க புள்ளி (since 2020)

title: 📘 Articles — A, An, The
content_text:
Articles are special adjectives used before nouns.

📌 INDEFINITE ARTICLES — A and AN (refer to any one, non-specific):
• A — before consonant sounds
  Examples: a book, a car, a university (u = "you" sound)
• AN — before vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u sounds)
  Examples: an apple, an hour (h is silent), an honest man, an MBA

📌 DEFINITE ARTICLE — THE (refer to specific, known thing):
• Used when both speaker and listener know which one
• Example: "I saw a dog. The dog was barking." (second mention)

Special uses of THE:
✅ Mountains, rivers, oceans: the Himalayas, the Ganga, the Pacific
✅ Unique things: the Sun, the Moon, the Earth
✅ Musical instruments: the guitar, the piano
✅ Superlatives: the best, the tallest
✅ Historical events: the World War

NO ARTICLE used:
❌ Proper nouns: Chennai, India, Ravi
❌ Plural general nouns: Dogs are loyal. (general)
❌ Uncountable general nouns: Water is essential.
tamil_translation:
Articles என்பவை பெயர்ச்சொல்களுக்கு முன் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் சிறப்பு சொற்கள்.

📌 A மற்றும் AN (Indefinite Articles):
• A — மெய்யெழுத்து ஒலியில் தொடங்கும் சொற்களுக்கு: a book, a car
• AN — உயிரெழுத்து ஒலியில் தொடங்கும் சொற்களுக்கு: an apple, an hour

📌 THE (Definite Article):
• குறிப்பிட்ட, தெரிந்த பொருள்களுக்கு
• மலைத்தொடர்கள், நதிகள்: the Himalayas, the Ganga
• தனிப்பட்டவை: the Sun, the Moon
• இசைக்கருவிகள்: the guitar, the piano
• மேலிட நிலை: the best, the tallest

❌ Article தேவையில்லை:
• சரியான பெயர்ச்சொற்கள்: Chennai, India
• பொதுவான பன்மை: Dogs are loyal.

title: 📘 Direct and Indirect Speech
content_text:
DIRECT SPEECH — The exact words of the speaker, placed within quotation marks.
Example: He said, "I am going to school."

INDIRECT SPEECH (Reported Speech) — Reporting what someone said without using their exact words.
Example: He said that he was going to school.

CHANGES IN INDIRECT SPEECH:

1. PRONOUNS change:
• "I" → he/she
• "we" → they
• "you" → I/he/she/they (depends on context)
• "my" → his/her

2. TENSES change (backshift):
• is/am/are → was/were
• will → would
• can → could
• may → might
• shall → should
• has/have → had
• was/were → had been

3. TIME EXPRESSIONS change:
• now → then
• today → that day
• yesterday → the previous day
• tomorrow → the next day/the following day
• here → there
• this → that / these → those
tamil_translation:
நேர்மொழி (Direct Speech) — பேசுபவரின் சரியான வார்த்தைகள், மேற்கோள் குறிகளுக்குள் வைக்கப்படும்.
ெ.கா: He said, "I am going to school."

மறைமொழி (Indirect/Reported Speech) — வேறொருவர் கூறியதை நம் வார்த்தைகளில் சொல்வது.
ெ.கா: He said that he was going to school.

மாறும் விஷயங்கள்:
1. பிரதிப்பெயர்கள்: "I" → he/she, "we" → they
2. காலங்கள்: is → was, will → would, can → could
3. நேர வெளிப்பாடுகள்: today → that day, tomorrow → the next day

title: ✏️ Reporting Questions and Commands
content_text:
REPORTING QUESTIONS:
• Yes/No questions → use "if" or "whether"
  Direct: "Are you coming?" he asked.
  Indirect: He asked if I was coming.

• Wh-questions → use the wh-word itself
  Direct: "Where do you live?" she asked.
  Indirect: She asked where I lived.

REPORTING COMMANDS:
• Positive command → told + to + verb
  Direct: "Sit down," the teacher said to us.
  Indirect: The teacher told us to sit down.

• Negative command → told + not to + verb
  Direct: "Do not make noise," she said.
  Indirect: She told them not to make noise.

REPORTING REQUESTS:
• requested + to + verb
  Direct: "Please help me," he said.
  Indirect: He requested me to help him.
tamil_translation:
கேள்வி வாக்கியங்களை மறைமொழியாக மாற்றுதல்:
• ஆம்/இல்லை கேள்விகள் → "if" அல்லது "whether" பயன்படுத்தவும்
  "Are you coming?" → He asked if I was coming.

• Wh-கேள்விகள் → அதே wh-word பயன்படுத்தவும்
  "Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.

கட்டளை வாக்கியங்கள்:
• நேர்மறை → told + to + verb
• எதிர்மறை → told + not to + verb

கோரிக்கை வாக்கியங்கள்:
• requested + to + verb

title: 📘 Active and Passive Voice
content_text:
ACTIVE VOICE — Subject performs the action.
Structure: Subject + Verb + Object
Example: "Priya writes a letter." (Priya is doing the writing)

PASSIVE VOICE — Subject receives the action. The focus is on what happened, not who did it.
Structure: Object + be verb + Past Participle + (by + Agent)
Example: "A letter is written by Priya."

PASSIVE VOICE FORMULA FOR EACH TENSE:

| Tense | Active | Passive |
| Simple Present | writes | is/am/are written |
| Present Continuous | is writing | is/am/are being written |
| Present Perfect | has written | has/have been written |
| Simple Past | wrote | was/were written |
| Past Continuous | was writing | was/were being written |
| Past Perfect | had written | had been written |
| Simple Future | will write | will be written |
| Future Perfect | will have written | will have been written |
tamil_translation:
கர்த்தரி வாக்கியம் (Active Voice) — கர்த்தா செயலை செய்கிறான்.
ெ.கா: "Priya writes a letter." (Priya எழுதுகிறாள்)

கர்மணி வாக்கியம் (Passive Voice) — செயல் செய்யப்படுகிறது என்று கூறுகிறது.
ெ.கா: "A letter is written by Priya."

கர்மணி உருவாக்கம்: Object + be verb + Past Participle + (by + Agent)

| காலம் | கர்த்தரி | கர்மணி |
| Simple Present | writes | is written |
| Simple Past | wrote | was written |
| Simple Future | will write | will be written |

title: ✏️ Step-by-Step Conversion
content_text:
HOW TO CONVERT ACTIVE TO PASSIVE — 4 Steps:

1. Find the OBJECT in the active sentence → it becomes the new SUBJECT
2. Choose the correct form of "be" (is/was/will be etc.)
3. Use the PAST PARTICIPLE of the main verb
4. Add "by + original subject" (if needed)

Example:
Active: "She teaches English."
Step 1: Object = English → becomes new subject
Step 2: Simple Present → is/am/are
Step 3: teach → taught
Step 4: by her
Passive: "English is taught by her." ✅

When to omit "by + agent":
• When the agent is unknown: "My wallet was stolen."
• When the agent is obvious: "Rice is grown in India."
• When the agent is unimportant
tamil_translation:
கர்த்தரியிலிருந்து கர்மணியாக மாற்றும் 4 படிகள்:

1. Active இல் Object ஐ கண்டுபிடிக்கவும் → இது புதிய Subject ஆகும்
2. சரியான "be" வினையை தேர்வு செய்யவும் (is/was/will be)
3. Main verb இன் Past Participle பயன்படுத்தவும்
4. "by + original subject" சேர்க்கவும்

ெ.கா:
Active: "She teaches English."
Passive: "English is taught by her." ✅

"by + agent" விட்டுவிடும்போது:
• செய்பவர் தெரியாதபோது: "My wallet was stolen."
• வெளிப்படையாக தெரியும்போது: "Rice is grown in India."

title: 📘 Conditional Sentences — If Clauses
content_text:
Conditional sentences express what will happen IF something else happens or happened.

ZERO CONDITIONAL — Universal truths and scientific facts
IF + Simple Present → Simple Present
Example: "If you heat water to 100°C, it boils."

FIRST CONDITIONAL — Real/possible future situations
IF + Simple Present → will + base verb
Example: "If it rains, we will stay indoors."
(This could actually happen)

SECOND CONDITIONAL — Imaginary/unlikely present/future situations
IF + Simple Past → would + base verb
Example: "If I were a bird, I would fly everywhere."
(Use "were" for all subjects with "I, he, she, it" in formal English)

THIRD CONDITIONAL — Imaginary past — what COULD HAVE happened but DIDN'T
IF + Past Perfect → would have + past participle
Example: "If she had studied, she would have passed."
(She didn't study, so she didn't pass — past regret)
tamil_translation:
நிபந்தனை வாக்கியங்கள் (Conditional Sentences) — "ஒன்று நடந்தால் மற்றொன்று நடக்கும்" என்று கூறுகிறது.

ZERO CONDITIONAL — பொதுவான உண்மைகள்/அறிவியல் உண்மைகள்
IF + Simple Present → Simple Present
ெ.கா: "If you heat water, it boils." (எப்போதும் உண்மை)

FIRST CONDITIONAL — நடக்கக்கூடிய எதிர்கால சாத்தியங்கள்
IF + Simple Present → will + base verb
ெ.கா: "If it rains, we will stay."

SECOND CONDITIONAL — கற்பனை/சாத்தியமற்ற சூழல்கள்
IF + Simple Past → would + base verb
ெ.கா: "If I were a bird, I would fly."

THIRD CONDITIONAL — கடந்தகால வருத்தங்கள்
IF + Past Perfect → would have + past participle
ெ.கா: "If she had studied, she would have passed."

title: 📘 Modal Verbs — Meaning and Usage
content_text:
Modal verbs are auxiliary (helping) verbs that express ability, possibility, permission, obligation, or advice.

Key Modals and their meanings:

| Modal | Main Meanings | Example |
| CAN | Ability (present) | She can swim. |
| COULD | Ability (past) / Polite request | He could run fast. / Could you help? |
| MAY | Permission (formal) / Possibility | May I come in? / It may rain. |
| MIGHT | Weak possibility | He might be at home. |
| SHOULD | Advice / Recommendation | You should exercise daily. |
| MUST | Strong necessity / Obligation | You must wear a helmet. |
| MUST NOT | Strong prohibition | You must not lie. |
| NEED NOT | Absence of necessity | You need not come early. |
| SHALL | Future (formal) / Offers | Shall we begin? |
| WOULD | Polite request / Habit in past | Would you like tea? / He would walk daily. |
| OUGHT TO | Moral obligation | We ought to respect elders. |
| USED TO | Past habit (no longer exists) | She used to play cricket. |
tamil_translation:
Modal verbs என்பவை திறன், சாத்தியம், அனுமதி, கட்டாயம் அல்லது அறிவுரையை வெளிப்படுத்தும் துணை வினைகள்.

| Modal | பொருள் | எ.கா |
| CAN | திறன் (நிகழ்காலம்) | She can swim. |
| COULD | திறன் (கடந்தகாலம்) | He could run fast. |
| MAY | அனுமதி / சாத்தியம் | May I come in? |
| MIGHT | மிதமான சாத்தியம் | He might be at home. |
| SHOULD | அறிவுரை | You should exercise. |
| MUST | கட்டாயம் | You must wear helmet. |
| WOULD | மரியாதையான கோரிக்கை | Would you like tea? |
| USED TO | கடந்தகால பழக்கம் | She used to play. |

title: 📘 Question Tags
content_text:
A Question Tag is a short question added at the end of a statement to seek confirmation or agreement.

GOLDEN RULE:
✅ POSITIVE statement → NEGATIVE tag
✅ NEGATIVE statement → POSITIVE tag

Structure: [Auxiliary verb + not + subject pronoun?] or [Auxiliary verb + subject pronoun?]

Examples:
• "She is a doctor, isn't she?" (positive → negative)
• "He hasn't eaten, has he?" (negative → positive)
• "They will come, won't they?" (positive → negative)
• "You don't like fish, do you?" (negative → positive)

SPECIAL CASES:
• "I am" → "aren't I?"
  "I am right, aren't I?"
• "Nobody/nothing/nowhere/never" (negative words) → positive tag with "they"
  "Nobody came, did they?"
• "Let's" → "shall we?"
  "Let's go, shall we?"
• Imperatives (command) → "will you?"
  "Open the door, will you?"
tamil_translation:
கேள்வி முனை (Question Tag) என்பது ஒரு வாக்கியத்தின் இறுதியில் உறுதிப்படுத்தல் அல்லது சம்மதம் தேட சேர்க்கப்படும் சிறு கேள்வி.

தங்க விதி:
✅ நேர்மறை வாக்கியம் → எதிர்மறை முனை
✅ எதிர்மறை வாக்கியம் → நேர்மறை முனை

ெ.கா:
• "She is a doctor, isn't she?"
• "He hasn't eaten, has he?"
• "They will come, won't they?"

சிறப்பு நிகழ்வுகள்:
• "I am" → "aren't I?"
• Nobody/nothing → did they?
• Let's → shall we?
• Command → will you?

title: 📘 Conditional Sentences — All Types Mastery
content_text:
COMPLETE GUIDE TO ALL 4 CONDITIONALS:

ZERO CONDITIONAL — Scientific facts and general truths
• If + S.P., S.P.
• "If you don't water plants, they die."
• "Water boils if you heat it to 100°C."

FIRST CONDITIONAL — Real, possible future
• If + S.P., will + base
• "If she works hard, she will succeed."
• "If it rains, the match will be cancelled."

SECOND CONDITIONAL — Imaginary present/future (unlikely or impossible)
• If + S.Past (were for all), would + base
• "If I were the president, I would build more schools."
• "If she knew the answer, she would tell us."

THIRD CONDITIONAL — Imaginary past (regrets/missed chances)
• If + Past Perfect, would have + P.P.
• "If I had saved money, I would have bought a house."
• "If she had come earlier, she would have met him."

INVERTED CONDITIONALS (without "if"):
• Were I → Second Conditional: "Were I rich, I would help them."
• Had I → Third Conditional: "Had I known, I would have told you."
• Should you → First Conditional: "Should you need help, call me."
tamil_translation:
அனைத்து நிபந்தனை வகைகளும்:

ZERO — பொதுவான உண்மைகள்: If + S.P., S.P.
FIRST — நடக்கக்கூடியது: If + S.P., will + base
SECOND — கற்பனை நிகழ்/எதிர்காலம்: If + S.Past, would + base
THIRD — கடந்தகால வருத்தம்: If + Past Perfect, would have + P.P.

"if" இல்லாமல் நிபந்தனை:
• Were I → Second: "Were I rich, I would help."
• Had I → Third: "Had I known, I would have told you."

title: 📘 Subject-Verb Agreement (Concord)
content_text:
Concord means that the VERB must agree with its SUBJECT in number (singular/plural) and person.

BASIC RULE:
• Singular Subject → Singular Verb (adds -s)
• Plural Subject → Plural Verb (no -s)
  "The boy runs." / "The boys run."

TRICKY RULES:

1. EACH / EVERY / EITHER / NEITHER → always SINGULAR
   "Each of the students has submitted."
   "Neither of them is ready."

2. BOTH / FEW / MANY / SEVERAL → always PLURAL
   "Both the girls are intelligent."

3. NEITHER...NOR / EITHER...OR → verb agrees with NEAREST subject
   "Neither Ravi nor his friends are coming."
   "Either the teachers or the principal is responsible."

4. COLLECTIVE NOUNS:
   • As one unit (singular): "The committee has decided."
   • As individuals (plural): "The committee are divided in opinion."

5. UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS → always SINGULAR
   "The news is shocking."
   "Mathematics is my favourite subject."

6. DISTANCES / TIME / MONEY / WEIGHT → SINGULAR
   "Ten kilometres is a long walk."
   "Five rupees is enough."
tamil_translation:
Concord என்பது வினை (verb) அதன் கர்த்தாவுடன் (subject) எண் மற்றும் ஆள்படையில் ஒத்திசைக்க வேண்டும் என்று சொல்கிறது.

அடிப்படை விதி:
• ஒருமை கர்த்தா → ஒருமை வினை (-s சேர்க்கவும்)
• பன்மை கர்த்தா → பன்மை வினை (-s இல்லாமல்)

கடினமான விதிகள்:
1. EACH / EVERY / EITHER / NEITHER → எப்போதும் ஒருமை
2. BOTH / FEW / MANY → எப்போதும் பன்மை
3. Neither...nor / Either...or → அருகில் உள்ள கர்த்தாவுடன் வினை
4. கூட்டுப் பெயர்ச்சொல் → அலகாக = ஒருமை, தனியாக = பன்மை
5. எண்ணிலடங்காப் பெயர்ச்சொல்கள் → எப்போதும் ஒருமை

title: 📘 Clauses — Noun, Adjective, Adverb
content_text:
A CLAUSE is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb.

1. NOUN CLAUSE — Acts like a noun in a sentence.
   • Used as subject, object, or complement.
   • Introduced by: that, what, why, how, whether, who
   • "I know that she is honest." (object noun clause)
   • "What he said is true." (subject noun clause)

2. ADJECTIVE CLAUSE (Relative Clause) — Modifies a noun.
   • Introduced by: who, whom, whose, which, that
   • "The boy who topped the exam is my friend."
   • "The book which you gave me is interesting."

3. ADVERB CLAUSE — Modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb.
   • Shows time, place, reason, condition, contrast, manner
   • TIME: "She cried when she heard the news." (when)
   • REASON: "He stayed home because he was sick." (because)
   • CONDITION: "If it rains, we will stay." (if)
   • CONTRAST: "Although she was tired, she worked." (although)
   • MANNER: "She spoke as if she knew everything." (as if)
tamil_translation:
திரட்சி (Clause) என்பது கர்த்தாவும் வினையும் உள்ள சொல் தொகுதி.

1. Noun Clause — பெயர்ச்சொல்லாக செயல்படும்
   • "I know that she is honest."
   • "What he said is true."

2. Adjective Clause — பெயர்ச்சொல்லை விவரிக்கும்

title: 📘 Error Spotting — 20 Golden Rules
content_text:
TOP 10 ERROR SPOTTING RULES FOR HSC:

1. ONE OF THE → plural noun after it
   ❌ one of the best student → ✅ one of the best students

2. DOUBLE COMPARATIVE → remove "more" before -er adjective
   ❌ more taller → ✅ taller

3. SINCE vs FOR → since = point in time, for = duration
   ❌ since three years → ✅ for three years
   ❌ for 2020 → ✅ since 2020

4. EACH/EVERY → always singular verb
   ❌ Each of them have submitted → ✅ has submitted

5. NEWS/MATHEMATICS/PHYSICS → uncountable, always singular
   ❌ The news are shocking → ✅ The news is shocking

6. THAN I vs THAN ME → use subject pronoun after "than"
   ❌ more senior than me → ✅ more senior than I

7. INDIRECT SPEECH TENSE → will → would in reported
   ❌ she said she will come → ✅ she said she would come

8. MISPLACED ONLY → place "only" before the word it modifies
   ❌ She only loves coffee → ✅ She loves only coffee

9. BETWEEN vs AMONG → between = 2, among = 3+
   ❌ distributed between five students → ✅ among

10. HARDLY/SCARCELY/BARELY → negative words, no double negative
    ❌ He could not hardly speak → ✅ He could hardly speak
